# You are performing an independent current-literature review of a two-paragraph s

**Question:** You are performing an independent current-literature review of a two-paragraph scientific summary describing PRIMARY (autoantibody-associated) MEMBRANOUS NEPHROPATHY. Do your own literature search; do not simply agree from memory. Evidence cutoff of the summary is 2026-10-13. Secondary membranous nephropathy (lupus/class V, malignancy, infection, drug-associated) and therapy efficacy are explicitly OUT OF SCOPE, so do not fault the summary for omitting them.

SUMMARY TO EVALUATE — Paragraph 1: "Within this bounded primary membranous nephropathy evidence, the disease is represented as one shared antigen-autoantibody mechanism rather than separate diseases per antigen. IgG4-predominant autoantibodies bind a podocyte surface antigen: PLA2R in most inspected adult cases, THSD7A in a smaller PLA2R-negative subgroup, and semaphorin 3B, HTRA1 or further mass-spectrometry targets in the remainder. In each instance the antigen was localized to podocytes or to the subepithelial deposits, and deposit-eluted IgG recognized it. Strong glomerular PLA2R staining tracked serum autoantibody, and HLA-DQA1 and PLA2R1 risk loci were associated with biopsy-proven disease in white-ancestry cohorts. Antigen-specific rodent models supply the directional evidence: podocyte expression of human PLA2R1 produced spontaneous antibodies, subepithelial deposits and nephrotic syndrome, lymphocyte-deficient animals developed neither, and Thsd7a-knockout mice were protected from antibody transfer. Complement activation and loss of slit-diaphragm proteins then accompany proteinuria."

Paragraph 2: "What remains uncertain is which complement route matters and how much complement is needed at all. All three initiation pathways were detected in patient biopsies, where proximity assays indicated classical-pathway dominance, yet factor-B-null mice were protected and lectin-pathway blockade preserved synaptopodin and NEPH1 in human podocyte culture; these assignments are mutually inconsistent and unresolved here. Effector evidence conflicts directly: terminal C5b-9 assembly was required for slit-protein proteolysis in culture and C5 deficiency partly reduced albuminuria, while membrane-attack-complex inhibition did not change albumin permselectivity on a glomerulus-on-a-chip, and anti-THSD7A antibodies caused proteolysis and slit-protein loss in C3-deficient mice. C3a/C3aR antagonism prevented proteinuria in one model. Antigen lumping asserts a shared route only, not shared frequency, serology or clinical associations: the putative targets reached under 1-4.9% of screened cases and some were index-case-only. All claims rest on agent-inspected abstracts; rodent and culture results are not human outcomes, no therapy is curated, and appraisals are uncalibrated."

TASKS — answer each explicitly and in order:
1. OVERALL VERDICT: choose exactly one of consistent_with_caveats / needs_revision / insufficient_evidence, and justify it.
2. MAJOR ERRORS: any statement that is factually wrong or unsupported by current literature.
3. OMISSIONS: important mechanisms or findings in current primary-MN understanding that a bounded summary of this kind should not omit (consider, among others: epitope spreading and anti-PLA2R titre as a severity/outcome correlate; IgG subclass switching; whether NELL1 and other antigens belong with the "primary" group; evidence on loss of tolerance/environmental triggers; podocyte-autonomous, complement-independent injury; whether "primary vs secondary" is still the right framing given antigen-based classification).
4. OUTDATED INTERPRETATIONS as of 2026.
5. CAUSAL OVERSTATEMENT: does the summary overstate causation anywhere, particularly in transferring rodent/transgenic and cell-culture results to human disease, or in the claim that antigens can be lumped into "one shared mechanism"?
6. UNRESOLVED DEBATES the summary gets right or wrong — especially which complement initiation pathway dominates in human MN, and whether C5b-9 is the principal effector of proteinuria.
7. SPECIFIC CORRECTIONS: concrete suggested rewordings, each with supporting citations.
Report your actual search coverage and the date range you searched. If you could not retrieve current literature for any part, say so explicitly rather than agreeing from memory.

# **Needs Revision** for primary membranous nephropathy, because the summary is broadly grounded but misclassifies antigens and overstates mechanistic unity.

The search covered four targeted literature queries on antigen classification, complement pathways, newer antigens, and PLA2R epitope/subclass biology, spanning papers published **2017-2025** with an evidence cutoff of **2026-10-13**. Current retrieval was strong for antigen classification, complement, and PLA2R biomarker biology, but sparse for some very recent niche mechanistic claims beyond the supplied 20 papers; where support was not retrievable here, that is stated explicitly.

## Primary Membranous Nephropathy

| Evidence Strength | Claim |
|---|---|
| Evidence strength: Strong (8/10) | Antigen discovery has **shifted MN classification** away from a simple primary-versus-secondary split toward an **antigen-based framework**, because different antigens carry different associations and phenotypes [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[3.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenic-spectrum-in-membranous-nephropathy-a-jain-tiwari/0f14bc45db215165b39c77afd0ad9815/) [[5.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/) |
| Evidence strength: Moderate (7/10) | **PLA2R** is the dominant adult antigen, but **NELL1, PCDH7, HTRA1, SEMA3B, CNTN1, FAT1, NTNG1, PCSK6, NDNF, and MPO** expand the spectrum, so “the remainder” is broader than the summary states [[6.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/altered-glycosylation-of-igg4-promotes-lectin-complement-haddad-lorenzen/a9c7d69bd3e65e64872dd647fb849374/) [[7.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/serine-protease-htra1-as-a-novel-target-antigen-in-primary-al-rabadi-caza/480a37a33e2e5bab819665430a134af2/) [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/) [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/) |
| Evidence strength: Moderate (6/10) | Complement evidence supports a role for **classical, lectin, and alternative pathways**, but the dominant initiating route and the necessity of **C5b-9** remain unresolved across human tissue, mouse, and cell systems [[9.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) [[9.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) [[10.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/) [[6.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/altered-glycosylation-of-igg4-promotes-lectin-complement-haddad-lorenzen/a9c7d69bd3e65e64872dd647fb849374/) [[9.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) |

**Figure 1:** Evidence strength for the summary’s main mechanistic claims

## Overall Verdict

**1. OVERALL VERDICT: needs_revision.** The summary gets the central autoimmune concept right: primary MN is usually antigen-specific autoimmunity against podocyte-associated targets, dominated by PLA2R and then THSD7A, with complement and podocyte structural injury implicated downstream [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-new-pathogenic-mechanisms-and-hoxha-reinhard/cca2dee3d424523fadbdeb86b2e8b858/) [[12.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[2.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[6.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/altered-glycosylation-of-igg4-promotes-lectin-complement-haddad-lorenzen/a9c7d69bd3e65e64872dd647fb849374/). But it needs revision because it treats antigen-defined MN too uniformly, omits now-important antigen reclassification, and excludes major current mechanistic qualifiers such as anti-PLA2R titre, epitope spreading, and antigen-based rather than primary/secondary framing [[3.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[8.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/) [[8.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/).

The biggest problem is not that the summary is wholly wrong, but that by 2025-2026 it is **too compressive** for a field that has moved toward antigen-specific heterogeneity. Reviews and cohorts now explicitly argue that antigens define partly distinct clinicopathologic entities, even if several share a podocyte autoantibody principle [[3.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[1.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[5.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/).

## Specific Issues

- **2. MAJOR ERRORS:** The statement that primary MN is best represented as “one shared antigen-autoantibody mechanism rather than separate diseases per antigen” is too strong against current antigen-based classification work, which argues the opposite at the clinicopathologic level [[3.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[3.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/).
- Calling the non-PLA2R/THSD7A remainder mainly **SEMA3B, HTRA1, or further mass-spectrometry targets** is incomplete and misleading because **NELL1** is now a major named antigen in that space, often around 5-10%, not a marginal afterthought [[12.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[12.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/).
- The phrase “putative targets reached under 1-4.9%” is factually wrong for **NELL1**, which multiple reviews place at roughly **5-10%** of MN cases, though not exclusively primary in every series [[12.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[12.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[8.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/).

- **3. OMISSIONS:** A bounded current summary should include that **anti-PLA2R levels correlate with disease activity** and often fall before proteinuria remits [[12.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[13.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[8.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/).
- It should include **epitope spreading**, because spread beyond the CysR domain associates with more severe disease and poorer remission prediction in newer studies [[8.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/) [[14.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/clinical-study-of-pla2r-epitope-spreading-for-predicting-cheng-zhou/4b527d33151e57d78883a054c66834a2/) [[15.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/quantitative-detection-and-prognostic-value-of-liu-xue/e98efc72d8095ae88aaac7d2a836a129/).
- It should note that antigen-specific IgG biology is not just “IgG4 predominant”; patients often also carry **IgG1-3**, and complement-activating subclasses matter mechanistically [[13.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[9.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/).

## Mechanistic Debates

**4. OUTDATED INTERPRETATIONS as of 2026:** The summary’s primary-versus-secondary framing is dated. Multiple papers argue this dichotomy has been overtaken by **molecular or antigen-based classification**, because the same antigen can occur with or without associated conditions [[1.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenic-spectrum-in-membranous-nephropathy-a-jain-tiwari/0f14bc45db215165b39c77afd0ad9815/). Its antigen list is also outdated because later reviews add **FAT1, NTNG1, PCSK6, NDNF, MPO** and other rare antigens beyond the earlier PLA2R/THSD7A/NELL1/SEMA3B/HTRA1 set [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/) [[5.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/).

**5. CAUSAL OVERSTATEMENT:** Yes. Rodent, transgenic, and cell-culture studies support pathogenic directionality, but they do not prove that all human primary MN shares one common effector route or one complement dependence [[11.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-new-pathogenic-mechanisms-and-hoxha-reinhard/cca2dee3d424523fadbdeb86b2e8b858/) [[9.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) [[9.6]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/). The strongest human claim is that primary MN is an antigen-specific autoimmune disease; the weaker claim is that all antigens can be safely lumped into one mechanistic disease model [[11.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-new-pathogenic-mechanisms-and-hoxha-reinhard/cca2dee3d424523fadbdeb86b2e8b858/) [[3.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/).

**6. UNRESOLVED DEBATES:** The summary is right that complement initiation remains debated. Human biopsy proximity assays support **classical-pathway predominance** in PLA2R- and THSD7A-associated MN, but lectin-pathway activation by aberrantly glycosylated **IgG4-MBL** interaction remains experimentally plausible, and alternative-pathway amplification is clearly important in at least one mouse model [[9.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) [[9.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/the-classical-pathway-triggers-pathogenic-complement-seifert-zahner/08101c1eee485710807642b1bed24280/) [[6.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/altered-glycosylation-of-igg4-promotes-lectin-complement-haddad-lorenzen/a9c7d69bd3e65e64872dd647fb849374/) [[10.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/). The summary is also right that **C5b-9 is not settled as the sole principal effector**: some models support it, but complement-independent podocyte injury and non-MAC pathways remain plausible from the mixed evidence presented here [[6.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/altered-glycosylation-of-igg4-promotes-lectin-complement-haddad-lorenzen/a9c7d69bd3e65e64872dd647fb849374/) [[10.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/alternative-pathway-is-essential-for-glomerular-luo-olaru/a1be865bb5c1564fa85a575acbfdac1c/) [[16.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/deposition-of-the-membrane-attack-complex-in-healthy-and-koopman-essen/463e9c73cb9151b39fa84a19cfdd220e/).

## Specific Corrections

1. Replace “**one shared antigen-autoantibody mechanism rather than separate diseases per antigen**” with: “Primary MN shares an antigen-specific podocyte autoantibody principle, but antigen-defined subtypes show distinct frequencies, IgG subclasses, and clinicopathologic associations.” [[3.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/new-antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-sethi/a67f7816cf3a5573b9d0ad50425b7338/) [[1.4]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[5.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/)

2. Replace the antigen sentence with: “PLA2R accounts for most adult antigen-associated cases, THSD7A for a smaller subset, and additional antigens include NELL1, SEMA3B, HTRA1, PCDH7, CNTN1 and other rarer targets.” [[12.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[12.3]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[7.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/serine-protease-htra1-as-a-novel-target-antigen-in-primary-al-rabadi-caza/480a37a33e2e5bab819665430a134af2/) [[5.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigens-in-membranous-nephropathy-discovery-and-sethi-fervenza/b42b76ab64105ab48649646227ea3278/)

3. Add: “In PLA2R-associated MN, **serum anti-PLA2R titre** tracks disease activity, often declines before proteinuria improves, and epitope spreading is associated with more severe disease and slower remission.” [[12.5]](https://consensus.app/papers/mechanisms-of-primary-membranous-nephropathy-gu-xu/e1981f32aab0500984ae1e093a4a2889/) [[13.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenspecific-igg-subclasses-in-primary-and-haxthausen-reinhard/d297a9b1108c5a34bf5123e9ebc7da34/) [[8.2]](https://consensus.app/papers/autoantibodies-in-the-diagnosis-monitoring-and-treatment-tesar-hruskova/982c1ecde4c055e486a864f94608d623/) [[17.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/role-of-pla2r-domain-antibodies-and-epitope-spreading-in-zhang-yang/e3e71dea874950cf95372705005d61ff/)

Replace “primary vs secondary” emphasis with: “Current literature increasingly favors an **antigen-based classification** that is then paired with associated conditions, rather than relying on a strict primary-secondary dichotomy.” [[1.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/membranous-nephropathy-current-understanding-of-various-ronco-dębiec/63f0efcbd3c05079b2c349cc01a7ec04/) [[2.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/a-target-antigenbased-approach-to-the-classification-of-bobart-tehranian/f465e38bf7e35f4198b90cfd301a5c1e/) [[4.1]](https://consensus.app/papers/antigenic-spectrum-in-membranous-nephropathy-a-jain-tiwari/0f14bc45db215165b39c77afd0ad9815/)

5.
